chunks.text: Chapter 1: overfitting. This synthetic handbook defines overfitting as memorizing training noise. The recommended intervention is regularization.

Table 3: overfitting benchmark. Headers: Approach | Accuracy percent | Training hours. Row: Model A | 77 | 5. Row: Model B | 81 | 3. Model B uses regularization. Values are synthetic, not scientific findings.

Figure 2: overfitting validation curve. Chart x-axis: epoch, y-axis: validation score. At epoch 1 the score is 5; at epoch 2 it is 14; at epoch 3 it is 8. The maximum is epoch 2. This is a visible-value transcription, not model-derived vision.
Chapter 5: applying overfitting. Workflow: normalize inputs, apply regularization, evaluate held-out examples. Do not select parameters using the evaluation labels.
Chapter 6: limitations of overfitting. The main drawback is high variance. Monitoring held-out results helps identify this tradeoff.
Appendix ZX-47: the overfitting maintenance record. Error code ZX-47 requires restarting the calibration stage. The calibration interval is 11 days. This identifier is case-insensitive.

Chapter 5: applying random forests. Workflow: normalize inputs, apply feature subsampling, evaluate held-out examples. Do not select parameters using the evaluation labels.
Chapter 6: limitations of random forests. The main drawback is limited interpretability. Monitoring held-out results helps identify this tradeoff.
